CHEMISTRY — TERMLY EXAM #6
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: CHEMISTRY
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2.? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2..
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2..
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2..
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2..

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Periodicity ● Trends in groups I, II, VII, VIII and period 3 ● gradation in size? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Periodicity ● Trends in groups I, II, VII, VIII and period 3 ● gradation in size.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Periodicity ● Trends in groups I, II, VII, VIII and period 3 ● gradation in size.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Periodicity ● Trends in groups I, II, VII, VIII and period 3 ● gradation in size.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Periodicity ● Trends in groups I, II, VII, VIII and period 3 ● gradation in size.

3. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. joule (J)
   C. newton (N)
   D. watt (W)

4. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Paper burning to ash

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Periodic Table ● Development of the periodic table . ● Ion formation . ● For? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Periodic Table ● Development of the periodic table . ● Ion formation . ● For.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Periodic Table ● Development of the periodic table . ● Ion formation . ● For.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on The Periodic Table ● Development of the periodic table . ● Ion formation . ● For.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Periodic Table ● Development of the periodic table . ● Ion formation . ● For.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Acids and Bases 2.2. Introduction to Salts 3.0 Organic Chemistry Page 15 of 40 1? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Acids and Bases 2.2. Introduction to Salts 3.0 Organic Chemistry Page 15 of 40 1.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Acids and Bases 2.2. Introduction to Salts 3.0 Organic Chemistry Page 15 of 40 1.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Acids and Bases 2.2. Introduction to Salts 3.0 Organic Chemistry Page 15 of 40 1.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Acids and Bases 2.2. Introduction to Salts 3.0 Organic Chemistry Page 15 of 40 1.

7. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 50 °C

8. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water always increases oxygen

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Chemical Bonding ● valence electron in bonding ● bond type (ionic, covalent, dat? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Chemical Bonding ● valence electron in bonding ● bond type (ionic, covalent, dat.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Chemical Bonding ● valence electron in bonding ● bond type (ionic, covalent, dat.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Chemical Bonding ● valence electron in bonding ● bond type (ionic, covalent, dat.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Chemical Bonding ● valence electron in bonding ● bond type (ionic, covalent, dat.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Chemistry? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Chemistry.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Chemistry.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Chemistry.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Chemistry.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Atom? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Atom.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Atom.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Atom.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on The Atom.

12. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Only carbon dioxide

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Acids and bases? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Acids and bases.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Acids and bases.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Acids and bases.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Acids and bases.

14. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

15. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Overgrazing continuously

16. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Chemical Bonding ● valence electron in bonding ● bond type (ionic, covalent, dat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Periodicity ● Trends in groups I, II, VII, VIII and period 3 ● gradation in size and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Acids and Bases 2.2. Introduction to Salts 3.0 Organic Chemistry Page 15 of 40 1 and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Acids and bases and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Salts ● Types of salts ● solubility of salts (chlorides, carbona and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Chemistry and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
